after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{-t}⟩$ at the point where $t=0.$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-{e}^{-t}⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =⟨-{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0),\,-{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0),\,-{e}^{-(0)}⟩ \\  & =⟨-0+1,\,-1-0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},\,-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},\,-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-{e}^{-t}⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =⟨-{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0),\,-{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0),\,-{e}^{-(0)}⟩ \\  & =⟨-0+1,\,-1-0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},\,-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},\,-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve   $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,,\,2{cos}^{2}⁡t⟩$  at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{6}.$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({cos}^{2}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-4\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{6},\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{6},\,-4\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{6}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{6}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-4\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-\sqrt{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+(-\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{4}+3} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $\frac{\pi }{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\text{ }⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-\sqrt{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4},\,-\frac{1}{4},\,-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t),z(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖

First, we find r′(t) and evaluate it at t=π6:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(sin⁡t),ddt(cos⁡t),2ddt(cos2⁡t)⟩=⟨cos⁡t,−sin⁡t,−4⋅cos⁡t⋅sin⁡t⟩r′(π6)=⟨cos⁡π6,−sin⁡π6,−4⋅cos⁡π6⋅sin⁡π6⟩=⟨32,−12,−4⋅32⋅12⟩=⟨32,−12,−3⟩

Now, we calculate the magnitude of r′(π6):

‖r′(π6)‖=(32)2+(−12)2+(−3)2=34+14+3=4=2 Finally, we normalize r′(π6) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where π6:
T(π6)=r′(π6)‖r′(π6)‖=12 ⟨32,−12,−3⟩=⟨34,−14,−32⟩

content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve   $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,,\,2{cos}^{2}⁡t⟩$  at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{6}.$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({cos}^{2}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-4\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{6},\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{6},\,-4\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{6}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{6}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-4\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-\sqrt{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+(-\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{4}+3} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $\frac{\pi }{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\text{ }⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-\sqrt{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4},\,-\frac{1}{4},\,-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=(t2+2)p(t) at the point corresponding to t=−1, given that p(−1)=i+2j−k and p′(−1)=i+j−k.

a
33(i−j−k)
b
33(−2i+3j−2k)
c
13(i−j−k)
d
66(−2i+j+k)
e
66(i+2j−k)
Submit

decision.explanation: By the product rule, r′(t)=2t p(t)+(t²+2)p′(t). Thus r′(−1)=−2(i+2j−k)+3(i+j−k)=i−j−k. Its magnitude is √3, so the unit tangent vector is (√3/3)(i−j−k), option a.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=({t}^{2}+2)p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=-1$, given that  $p(-1)=i+2\,j-k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(-1)=i+\,j-\,k.$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=-1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(({t}^{2}+2)p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+2)\cdot p(t)+({t}^{2}+2)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =2t\,p(t)+({t}^{2}+2)\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(-1) & =2(-1)\,p(-1)+((-1)^{2}+2)\,{p}^{′}(-1) \\  & =-2\,p(-1)+3\,{p}^{′}(-1) \\  & =-2(i+2\,j-k)+3(i+\,j-\,k) \\  & =-2i-4\,j+2k+3i+3j-3\,k \\  & =i-j-k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(1)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(-1)}{‖{r}^{′}(-1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot (i-j-k) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}(i-j-k)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=-1$ is  $T(-1)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}(i-j-k).$

content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=-1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(({t}^{2}+2)p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+2)\cdot p(t)+({t}^{2}+2)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =2t\,p(t)+({t}^{2}+2)\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(-1) & =2(-1)\,p(-1)+((-1)^{2}+2)\,{p}^{′}(-1) \\  & =-2\,p(-1)+3\,{p}^{′}(-1) \\  & =-2(i+2\,j-k)+3(i+\,j-\,k) \\  & =-2i-4\,j+2k+3i+3j-3\,k \\  & =i-j-k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(1)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(-1)}{‖{r}^{′}(-1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot (i-j-k) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}(i-j-k)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=-1$ is  $T(-1)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}(i-j-k).$

Question 5
?

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=tan⁡tp(t) at the point corresponding to t=π4, given that p(π4)=i−32j+32k and p′(π4)=3k.

a
 221i−321j+2321k
b
 221i−521j+2321k
c
 23i−23j+33k
d
 45i−15j+25k
e
25i−35j+235k
Submit

decision.explanation: The product rule gives r′(t)=sec²(t)p(t)+tan(t)p′(t). At t=π/4, this is 2p(π/4)+p′(π/4)=2i−3j+2√3k. Its magnitude is √(4+9+12)=5, so dividing by 5 gives option e.

after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$, given that  $p(\frac{\pi }{4})=i-\frac{3}{2}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=\sqrt{3}\,k.$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$

content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$, given that  $p(\frac{\pi }{4})=i-\frac{3}{2}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=\sqrt{3}\,k.$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{tan}⁡t)\cdot p(t)+\operatorname{tan}⁡t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡t\,p(t)+\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})p(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}){p}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =2(i-\frac{3}{2}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k)+(1)(\sqrt{3}\,k) \\  & =(2\,i-3\,j+\sqrt{3}\,k)+\sqrt{3}\,k \\  & =2\,i-3\,j+2\sqrt{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(2\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+9+12} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (2\,i-3\,j+2\sqrt{3}\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\,i-\frac{3}{5}\,j+\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is
 $T(\frac{\pi }{4})=\frac{2}{5}\,i-\frac{3}{5}\,j+\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}\,k.$
